artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>3$ be a prime. Denote by $\binom{3k}{k,k,k}=\frac{(3k)!}{(k!)^3}$ the trinomial (multinomial) coefficient, by $\binom{n}{m}$ the usual binomial coefficient, by $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ the $k$-th Catalan number, and by $\left(\frac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ the Legendre/Jacobi symbol. Prove or disprove the following three statements.

(i) One has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{1}{24^{k}}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}\equiv\begin{cases}\binom{2(p-1)/3}{(p-1)/3}\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 1\pmod 3,\\[4pt]\dfrac{p}{\binom{2(p+1)/3}{(p+1)/3}}\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }p\equiv 2\pmod 3.\end{cases}$$

(ii) Suppose $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$ and write $4p=x^{2}+27y^{2}$ with $x\equiv 2\pmod 3$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k+2}{24^{k}}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}\equiv x\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(iii) Furthermore,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{3k}{k}\,C_{k}}{24^{k}}\equiv \frac{1}{\binom{2(p-(p/3))/3}{(p-(p/3))/3}}\pmod p,$$
where $(p/3)$ denotes the Legendre symbol of $p$ modulo $3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search results suggest that parts of this set of conjectures of Z.-W. Sun (involving the sum of $\binom{3k}{k,k,k}/24^k$ modulo $p^2$) have been addressed in subsequent work by C. Wang, Z.-W. Sun and others, but no single source clearly confirms that all three parts (i), (ii), (iii) have been completely proved. The exact current status of each part could not be definitively verified.
